paragraphs: Mar son of Rav Ashi, who sealed the Babylonian Talmud. See Tavyomi, who sealed it. He said, 'That statement of Father's belongs to his youth': he said it when young, and objections can be raised against it, Gittin 29b. Rav Ashi said, etc.; rather, Mar son of Rav Ashi said, Yesh Noḥalin 122b. Rav Aḥa of Difti and Rav Yehudah bar Meremar were equal in wisdom [the terse relation is preserved]. Ravina found Mar son of Rav Ashi and told him, 'Let the master act,' Berakhot 36a. Rav Mordekhai lived in his generation. He put a demon under a ban to make it pay for the damage it caused, Ḥullin 105b. The law follows Mar son of Rav Ashi except in reversal of an oath and admission; some read 'and ḥivvarei,' there 76b; some read 'The law does not follow him, etc., except, etc.' See Tosafot Yoma 83; Ketubbot 96a, 'A widow'; Sanhedrin 29b; Ḥullin there; Shevuot 41a. Rif, Zeh Borer, writes in Rav Hai Gaon's name: wherever it does not explicitly say the law does not follow Mar son of Rav Ashi, it follows him. Throughout the Gemara we found only these two exceptions: reversal of an oath and ḥivvara [the whiteness of the sinews]; mnemonic: 'reversed white.' End of quotation. [Competing lists are retained, not reconciled.]
